contexts.text: Their fat () = the Celestial itself, which is of the Lord.
All these (celestial things) were represented by the fats in the sacrifices, Enumerated.
Therefore the Jewish people were forbidden to eat any fat from beasts.
That fatness = celestial things, and the goods of charity. Illustrated.
Fatness is not meant, but celestial spiritual good.
Fatness () = the Celestial which is of love.
My soul shall be satisfied with fat and fatness () = what is celestial.
Hence the firstfruits of the earth were called fatness.
The goods of love, of which a fat (pasture) is predicated (). AC 415:2.
See Butter, Milk, and Oil.
Fat things, and marrowy ones = goods.
God give thee... of the fatnesses of the earth () = from the Divine good.
Of the fatnesses of the earth shall be thy dwelling () = life from Divine good.
Fat in flesh () = which are of charity. Fat, or fatness = what is celestial, and is predicated of the good which is of love and charity.
Fat and good () = into which the things of faith and charity can be applied. Fat, when predicated of the scientifics signified by the ears of corn, = things receptible of the good of faith...
Ye shall eat the fat of the land () = the appropriation of good there.

Fat-pingue- = what is celestial, or good... not only the fat which is in an animal, but also the fat from any other source; as butter, oil: and the things which derive anything from fat = good in proportion as they derive from it; as milk, honey, gum.

That fatness was a representative of celestial good, thus of the love which is from the Lord, is evident from the burnt-offerings and sacrifices, in that all the fat was burnt upon the altar; and that there was from it an odour of rest to Jehovah; and also from the fact that the sons of Israel were forbidden to eat fat. AC 5943:3, Illustrated.
The fat and its being burnt = the veriest Divine Celestial itself, which is the good of love from the Lord. Illustrated.
Fatnesses = the goods of love and of charity.
As fatness = good, it is adjoined to such things as are not fat in themselves, but which = goods; thus fat-pingue- and good are as it were the same thing. Illustrated.

His bread fat () = delight from good. Fat = delight; for fatness = what is celestial, or the good of love; but when fat-pingue- is mentioned and is joined to bread, which = the good of love, then fat-pingue- = the delight which is of that love. AE 438:4.
To eat the flesh of the fat () = to turn good into evil.
Under Fatted, see this reference.
To make fat the head with oil () = to endow with celestial good.
The Jews forbidden to eat fat and blood () = lest they should profane holy things; for fat = Divine good; and blood, Divine truth.
Things fat and splendid () = celestial and spiritual affections of good and truth. ( = goods and truths, and happy and magnificent things. AE 1159.)
That fat things = celestial goods and their affections and delights of affections. Illustrated.
Fat in mind.
A feast of fat things = the appropriation and communication of goods.
To bring burnt-offerings of fat things = worship from the good of celestial love.
Fatnesses of the earth = the celestial things which are of the good of love.
The head of the valley of the fat ones () = the intelligence of the natural man.
Under Egypt, see this reference. AE 627:13. AE 654:21.
Fatness () = the good of love.
To be delighted in fatness () = to be delighted from good. ( = to be in happiness and blessedness. AE 1159:2.)
Fat and wealthy () = full of the good of love and of the truths thence derived.
The reason fat things = goods and the happinesses thence, is that the fatness is the best of the flesh; and because it is like oil, which = the good of love. Illustrated.
A feast of fat things, of fat things full of marrow = good both natural and spiritual with joy of heart.
Fats, in the opposite sense, = those who nauseate good, and who despise and reject it very much. Illustrated.
